documents: Kou et al. 2022, Acta Geologica Sinica (English Edition) 96(6): 1917-1931, published PDF (supplementary tables not supplied)

entry.evidence: Therefore, the time when remote effect of northeastward extrusion of the Tibetan Plateau reached Niushou Mountains

steps.action: Pose the unsolved question of when the far-field effect of the Tibetan Plateau's NE expansion reached the leading (NE) edge of the arcuate tectonic belt, because prior structural studies give no accurate time limit.
steps.quote: the time when remote effect of northeastward extrusion of the Tibetan Plateau reached Niushou Mountains

steps.action: Design and drill the 420.11 m HSB-1 core through the late Cenozoic alluvial fan in front of the Daluo Mountains to record the uplift-related sedimentary sequence.
steps.quote: The purpose of the drill was to reveal the detailed sedimentary sequence and stratigraphic framework corresponding to the uplift of the Daluo Mountains

steps.action: Log the core: fluvial sand, silt and clay below an unconformity at ~156.49 m, alluvial-fan conglomerates of local argillaceous siltstone clasts above.
steps.quote: a notable transformation from fluvial facies in the lower part to alluvial facies in the upper part

steps.action: Select samples: three conglomerate levels for 26Al/10Be burial dating, two sands for OSL, and two core gravels plus two outcrop source rocks (Daluo Ordovician, Yantong Carboniferous) for detrital zircon U-Pb.
steps.quote: These samples were analyzed to determine the precise age of the gravel from the alluvial fan and then the initiation time.

steps.action: Check LA-ICP-MS U-Pb calibration with the external standard 91500 and the secondary reference zircon GJ-1, whose measured ages match the reference age.
steps.quote: which are within the standard error relative to the reference age of 599.8 ± 1.7 Ma

steps.action: Describe thin sections: the lower core gravel (HSB-ZR-1) resembles the Yantong Carboniferous outcrop, and the upper gravel (HSB-ZR-2) resembles the Daluo Ordovician outcrop.
steps.quote: HSB-ZR-2 (Fig. 5c, d) appeared the same as DLS-ZR (Fig. 5g, h) under the microscope

steps.action: Obtain detrital zircon U-Pb age spectra (>90% concordant analyses) and age peaks for the two core gravels and the two outcrop samples.
steps.quote: The detrital zircon U-Pb dating yielded five age peaks at ~446 Ma, ~961 Ma, ~1029 Ma, ~1191 Ma, and ~2531 Ma

steps.action: Compute cosmogenic burial ages (~4.64, ~0.76, ~0.60 Ma) under stated burial-model assumptions and half-lives, and OSL ages (54.12 ± 6.39 and 50.51 ± 6.27 ka) for the upper sands.
steps.quote: The weighted ages of the samples DSL-1, DSL-2, and DSL-3 were ~4.64 Ma, ~0.76 Ma, and ~0.60 Ma, respectively.

steps.action: Compare core-gravel lithology and zircon spectra with the source outcrops: basal gravels match the Yantong Carboniferous (~450 Ma peak) and higher gravels match the Ordovician Miboshan Formation (~889-976 Ma peaks).
steps.quote: which is identical to the Carboniferous rocks at the Yantong Mountains in terms of both lithology and detrital zircon U-Pb age spectra

steps.action: Infer that the fluvial-to-fan transition marks the onset of uplift and that the provenance switch records erosion of the Paleozoic cover, and date the onset by the ~4.64 Ma basal burial age.
steps.quote: the development of the alluvial fan indicates the beginning of the late Cenozoic uplift of the Daluo Mountains

steps.action: Take from published work the ~5.4 Ma basal fan conglomerate of the Sikouzi section (Liupan Mountains) and the regional early Pliocene uplift, hiatus and cooling records.
steps.quote: a conglomerate at the bottom of the late Cenozoic alluvial fan deposited at ~5.4 Ma

steps.action: Compare the ~4.64 Ma onset with Sikouzi (~5.4 Ma) to derive a ~0.8 Myr propagation from the trailing to the leading edge of the belt, and relate it to regional hiatuses and ~5 Ma cooling.
steps.quote: commenced approximately 0.8 Myr later than Liupan Mountains

steps.action: Take from published work the Kunhuang and Gonghe movements and the ages of seven Yellow River terraces.
steps.quote: seven main terraces were formed in the upper reaches of the Yellow River

steps.action: Match the ca. 0.76-0.6 Ma and ~0.05 Ma gravel layers to the 0.6-0.5 Ma and ~0.05 Ma terraces and assign them to the Kunhuang and Gonghe movements.
steps.quote: it can be deduced that these two tectonic uplift episodes correspond to the Kunhuang and Gonghe movements

steps.action: Use the Hongsibao basin unconformity (ca. 0.054-0.035 Ma; Cui et al. 2018, co-authors' earlier work) and the Jilantai-Hetao lake retreat (Chen et al. 2008) as independent records.
steps.quote: [...] between the early Pleistocene Salawusu Formation and Shuidonggou Formation is indicative of a hiatus at ca. 0.054–0.035 Ma

steps.action: Note that the unconformity age agrees with the ~0.05 Ma gravel layer.
steps.quote: the formation time of this unconformity is consistent with the ~0.05 Ma gravel layer

steps.action: Reject climate change as the cause of the ~0.05 Ma terraces, gravels and unconformity in favour of a far-field tectonic uplift, by assertion without a stated test.
steps.quote: These phenomena cannot be explained by climate change and likely resulted from the remote effect of the tectonic uplift

steps.action: Conclude that the Daluo uplift began at ~4.64 Ma, with two Pleistocene uplift episodes at ca. 0.76-0.6 Ma and ~0.05 Ma.
steps.quote: indicates that start of the late Cenozoic uplift of the Daluo Mountains, which can be constrained to ~4.64 Ma

tree.answer: Late Cenozoic uplift of the Daluo Mts, recorded by alluvial-fan development over fluvial strata
No; read from traces in a drill core and dated sediments
Date the onset and key Pleistocene stages of uplift
No rivals stated before the test; climate change is dismissed only at the end
Conditions found, not set: a single core plus outcrop source samples
Only analytical standards checked; no robustness test of the ages or of the facies interpretation
Onset at ~4.64 Ma and two Pleistocene episodes kept by correlation with regional records

end.claim: The onset of alluvial-fan deposition over fluvial strata marks the start of late Cenozoic uplift of the Daluo Mountains at ~4.64 Ma, followed by two Pleistocene uplift episodes at ca. 0.76-0.6 Ma and ~0.05 Ma.

decisive_move.sentence: The 26Al/10Be burial age of ~4.64 Ma for the basal fan conglomerate (DSL-1), without which the uplift onset would be undated.

gates.evidence: The drill was sited to record uplift-related deposition (p. 1919), but no hypothesis with distinct predictions directed it. The interpretation that fan onset equals uplift is assumed rather than tested. The climate rival is rejected by assertion (p. 1928). Nothing is stated as fixed before the data.

imports.item: 10Be and 26Al half-lives and accelerator mass spectrometry for burial dating
Optically stimulated luminescence, single-aliquot regenerative dose protocol
LA-ICP-MS (New Wave UP213 laser with Agilent 7500a) for zircon U-Pb

novelty_claims.quote: This study provides a new time scale for the uplift and expansion of the arcuate tectonic belt
provide new evidences for discussion about the initial timing of the late Cenozoic uplift of Daluo Mountains

limits: Burial ages are reported in the main text without uncertainties; Supp. Tables 5-6 were not supplied. The burial-model assumptions (short pre-burial exposure, steady production) are stated but not tested. The equation of fan onset with tectonic uplift is assumed. Each Pleistocene episode rests on one or two samples. The climate-change rival is dismissed without analysis. Sub-claims: (a) the ~0.8 Myr propagation from Liupan to Daluo is a best_explanation resting on two dates, one cited; (b) the correspondence of the Pleistocene episodes to the Kunhuang and Gonghe movements is a best_explanation by temporal correlation only; (c) the provenance switch from Carboniferous to Ordovician sources is a best_explanation from zircon spectra and petrography. Internal tensions (inference): the provenance switch is said to indicate uplift 'during the early Miocene' (p. 1926), which conflicts with a Pliocene onset. Fig. 9a puts fluvial facies before ~5.4 Ma while the onset is ~4.64 Ma. The Qingshuiying Formation is called both Eocene and Oligocene (p. 1919). No review file was supplied, so the process behind the published version is unknown.
